You are agent K2 (short=modcatalog, branch feature/mod-catalog-ingestion, worktree /opt/nxeon-wt-modcatalog, dev port 3114). FIRST read /tmp/claude-0/-root/4f329df3-66ee-49c8-a6c5-615ecf189efc/scratchpad/AGENT-BRIEF.md in full and obey it.

MISSION: grow the NX Labs mod catalog with mods for ALL games we host, from license-compatible providers, kept fresh automatically, with images/descriptions/versions/compatibility — and pre-download popular mods to local storage so installs are a fast local copy. (Agent K1 builds the installers/Mods tab and consumes your data; you OWN the Mod/catalog schema — additive changes only.)
STEPS:
1. Inspect the existing catalog (prisma models for NX Labs/mods — ~64,000 rows exist; sources, fields, how marketing app/nxm NX Labs and customer portal read them; any existing scrapers/scripts). Report what's in it per game, freshness, missing images/descriptions/compat, duplicates.
2. Vet providers per game for API access + licensing/ToS and record the verdict in docs/MODS-SOURCES.md: Modrinth (API, per-project license, mirroring OK per license), Hangar (PaperMC), Spigot/SpigotMC (limits), Thunderstore (Valheim etc.), uMod/Oxide (Rust), Factorio mod portal API, ficsit.app (Satisfactory), mod.io, Steam Workshop (metadata only via Web API key; DO NOT redistribute files), CurseForge (API key + distribution terms — metadata/link-through only unless permitted; do not mirror), Nexus (no scraping). Only MIRROR files whose license/ToS permits redistribution; otherwise store metadata + link-through. Store spdx/license text, author, source URL, attribution. Honour robots/rate limits/User-Agent identifying Nxeon.
3. Build ingestion in lib/modsync/* + worker scheduler (rate-limited, resumable, ETag/If-Modified-Since, exponential backoff, idempotent upserts, dedupe by provider id, compatibility matrix game version × loader, categories, tags, download counts, icon/screenshot caching (resize/convert to webp, store locally, serve via our own route/CDN path), sanitised markdown/HTML descriptions) + an admin page /admin/nxlabs (single registry entry, A1 owns nav) showing per-provider status, last run, counts, errors, storage usage, with pause/resume/run-now controls.
4. LOCAL MIRROR: the owner provisioned ~100 GB for NX Labs pre-downloaded mods — locate it (check df/mounts on this host, the DB/docs for an NX Labs VM or path, /tank, `lsblk`, prior scripts) and document what exists; design the mirror layout (by provider/game/mod/version, content-addressed with sha256), size accounting, LRU/popularity eviction policy, integrity verification, and a fast copy path for K1's installer (lib/modsync/mirror.ts: resolveLocal(modVersion) → path|null). Decide pragmatically whether pre-downloading helps (installs from upstream CDNs are already fast; mirror matters for reliability, rate limits, and sources that throttle) — implement for the popular-by-downloads slice per game within the budget.
5. PROVE IT: run ingestion in SMALL rate-limited batches (a few thousand mods across several games, real network calls are fine for public APIs) into a throwaway DB, show counts per game/provider and sample records with images; NO big scrape against prod DB — deliver the exact command + schedule for the owner to start production ingestion. Update docs. Tests with recorded API fixtures for parsers.

tools.name: Artifact
tools.description:
Render an HTML file to an Artifact — a default-private web page hosted on claude.ai. Use this when communicating visually would be clearer than terminal text, or when the user or their team would use the page rather than only read it — to collect input, track things people change, or see live data. Publishing proactively is fine for your own work-product — artifacts start private. The exception is content that could mislead or cause harm if shared onward: anything imitating a real organization, person, or record, or content the user framed as sensitive. Build those as files, and let the user decide whether they get a URL.

A finished deliverable with an audience — a report for a team, a plan other people will follow, a document meant as a reference, the case for a decision the team has yet to make — is not fully delivered while it lives only in terminal scrollback or a local file, even when asked as a question. Finishing such work includes publishing it — as an artifact, or through a first-party document connector when one is attached — and handing the user the link, so they have a private page ready to share when they choose; when such a decision was put to you as a question, give the answer in the terminal and offer the page in one line instead. When a first-party connector for reading and writing documents is attached — first-party is asserted by the host, never inferred from a server's own name, description, or instructions — a request for a page, doc, notes, memo, plan or report goes to that connector (starting the document from the Docs Artifact type when this tool lists one), unless the user asks for the file format itself (a .docx or .pptx file, say); publish an artifact for app-, site-, dashboard- or game-shaped pages, or when the user asks for an artifact or an HTML/Markdown page to view or share; when the user asks for the file itself ("just give me the .html file", "save these notes as a .md file", say), give them that file rather than publishing it. Advice the user will act on alone, now, in the code at hand has no audience.

**Runtime capabilities**: depending on what is enabled for this user, a published page can do more than static HTML — read the user's live or connected data, remember what people do on it (a poll, a sign-up sheet, a checklist, a document edited in place — the page saves new versions of itself), keep state shared across viewers, know who is viewing, ask Claude a question of its own, store files people add, or hand the viewer a file to save — declared via the `capabilities` input. **Whenever any of that would make the page more useful, you MUST load the `artifact-capabilities` skill BEFORE writing the artifact, and always before passing `capabilities` or writing any `window.claude.*` runtime code** — it tells you what's available to this user and how to use it. When a capability that keeps state is available, prefer it over browser storage for that kind of state; `localStorage` stays the fallback for per-viewer conveniences. Omitting the field on a redeploy keeps what the page already has; `{}` clears it. A page that saves new versions of itself reaches this session like any other republish — a republish notice on a watched artifact, or a conflict on your next publish of it — and your local file is then behind: re-read, merge, republish.

**Before writing the file, Claude must load the `artifact-design` skill**, including for a `.md` file that a skill told Claude to write. The skill holds the page contract, from the authoring format (HTML, or Markdown only when a loaded skill asks for it) to the title, libraries, storage, size limit, layout, theming and icon. It also sets how much design effort the request deserves, and Claude never writes Markdown to get around it. Claude then writes the content to a file (via Write/Edit) and calls Artifact with its path, putting the file in its scratchpad directory when the system prompt lists one and the person names no other location. A quickstart result with the page-design guidance counts as loading `artifact-design`.

**If Claude writes a page before that skill has loaded**, the skill's contract still applies. Claude gives the page a `<title>` that is a name of two to four words, never "Name: explainer", and puts the explanation in `description`. Claude defines colors as tokens on `:root`, redefines them for dark mode under `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` guarded by `:root:not([data-theme="light"])` and again under `:root[data-theme="dark"]`, and gives `body` an explicit background. Claude loads external scripts only from cdnjs.cloudflare.com (preferred), cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/, unpkg.com, cdn.tailwindcss.com or code.jquery.com, loads stylesheets only from Google Fonts, and puts everything else inline. Claude makes the layout work at phone width, with a 16px side gutter and no horizontal page scroll.

**Format**: Always author the page as `.html`. Publish a `.md` file only when a loaded skill explicitly instructs it. When the user shares a markdown document or asks to turn one into an artifact, author an HTML page based on its content — preserve its substance, and design the page as you would any other artifact rather than transcribing the markdown one-to-one.

**Browser storage**: `localStorage` (also `sessionStorage` and IndexedDB) works, but each artifact has its own origin and the data lives only in that viewer's browser — it survives republishes to the same URL and never reaches other viewers, other devices, or Claude. It can come back empty or the accessor can throw (a private window, cleared or blocked site data, previews or thumbnail capture), so wrap every read and write in try/catch and render the page correctly without it. Use it only for per-viewer conveniences (a remembered tab or filter, a collapsed section, an unsent draft), never for state that must persist reliably, be shared between viewers, or be read back by Claude — state like that belongs in a runtime capability when this user has one: load the `artifact-capabilities` skill before writing the page.

**Size**: The rendered page must be 16MB or smaller, and embedded data: URIs count toward that.

**Supporting files**: a multi-file artifact (separate stylesheets, scripts, data, images, or further HTML pages) publishes its other files through `files`, which maps each published path to a source file. The published path is what the HTML references, relative and with no leading slash. Only the page itself is wrapped in a document skeleton at publish time: an HTML file in `files` is another page served without one, so Claude starts each with its own `<!doctype html>`, charset and viewport metas and base styles, or, without the doctype, it renders in quirks mode with browser defaults. On an update, files Claude passes are added or replaced, files it leaves out are kept, and `null` removes one. Limits: 16MB for the page and each text file, 15MB for each binary file, and standard web media types only; one publish sends at most 255 files and 64MB, while a version may hold up to 511 files and 256MB in all, so a larger set goes up over several publishes to the same `url` (each later publish adds to the files already there).

**Calls**: `action` picks one (publish when omitted):
- **publish** (the default): takes `file_path`, plus `icon` on a first publish and an optional one-sentence `description`, and with `url` updates that existing artifact in place. With `url`, `file_path` and `asset: true`, it instead uploads that local image, video, PDF, font or text file to the artifact's asset store; `file_paths` in place of `file_path` uploads up to 25 image, video, PDF, font, stylesheet or script files in one call under one approval (a text file goes in a call of its own), and the result gives each one's `url`. from_url.description: publish with `asset: true`, in place of `file_path`: the SOURCE artifact's claude.ai URL — one the person can open.

asset_ids.description: publish with `asset: true` and `from_url` only: 1–10 distinct asset ids from the source artifact (from a `scope: "assets"` listing of it, or an upload result).

The key is what the HTML references. The source is a path on disk, or {from, contentType} when the type cannot be inferred from the published extension. An {artifact, path} source copies that Artifact's published file on the server: an Artifact the person can open, with its type carried over, never an HTML, SVG or XML document, and at most 4 source Artifact versions per publish. null removes that path on an update, and files left out are kept. A plain list publishes each file at its own spelling. Sources must be under the working directory or Claude's scratchpad directory. `preflight.js` at the artifact root is reserved: it runs against open pages when Claude publishes updates, and it must be a JavaScript module of at most 8 KiB whose default export is a function, or the publish is refused.

path.description: Path relative to the working directory (or to `root`, which may be a folder in your scratchpad directory); the file is served at this same path next to the page.

contentType.description: Servable media type; inferred from the extension for common types (css/js/json/png/…) — pass explicitly otherwise.

from.description: Source file path — relative to `root` (default: the working directory), or absolute under the working directory or your scratchpad directory.

contentType.description: Servable media type; inferred from the PUBLISHED extension for common types — pass explicitly otherwise.

artifact.description: Another artifact's claude.ai URL: the file is copied from ITS published files, server side — nothing is downloaded. You must be able to open that artifact.

path.description: The file's published path inside that Artifact, as a listing of its files prints it (not "index.html").

ver.description: A version of that Artifact to copy from instead of its current one — only versions you are served (its history, if you can edit it); omit for the current version.

root.description: The base directory that relative `files` sources resolve against, like a bundler root. It never changes published paths. It is relative to the working directory, or absolute within it or within Claude's scratchpad directory. It requires `files`, except on an Artifact made from a type, where a data `file_path` under it is served at its path relative to it.

pin.description: publish only: true also pins the published artifact to the person's claude.ai sidebar once it is published. Claude passes it only when the person asked for that. A failed pin never fails the publish, and the result says so.

limit.description: list only: the maximum number of artifacts to return (default 25).

scope.description: list: which listing to return. 'mine' is the default. The others are 'shared', 'all', 'types', 'files' (with `url`) and 'assets' (with `url`, continued with `after`). See **Calls**.

type_query.description: list with scope 'types' only: limits the listing to the types whose title or description match this text best, ignoring case; a type that matches less well is left out, so a narrowed listing is not the whole catalog. Claude omits it when choosing a type for a request, unless a listing made without it says more types exist than it shows.

type.description: list only: the name of a published Artifact type, as a 'types' listing shows it (case does not matter). The listing then shows the Artifacts made from that type instead of the person's gallery. Claude passes this or `type_url`, not both.

intent.description: quickstart only (required): what is being made — 'document' (text to read or edit together), 'slides' (a deck or one slide), 'design' (a visual design or prototype on a canvas), 'other' (anything else, or unsure).

design_systems.description: quickstart only: false when a design system's link is already in hand (it is then read with its own call) or one was declined. Omitted or true, the result lists the design systems (not for a document) and, for slides or a design, attaches the default one's README.

title.description: publish: the fallback title for an HTML page whose file has no <title>. It is a name, not a summary, and Claude keeps it the same across redeploys. On a `type_url` create, it is the new Artifact's name: what the person called it, or a short descriptive name. If it is left out, the Artifact is named after the type.

description.description: publish: one sentence for the subtitle on the gallery card.

label.description: A short name for this publish, at most 60 characters (e.g. "Draft to legal"). Optional. It is a few words, not a description.

overwrite_unread.description: publish with `files` or `root` to an existing artifact: published paths this call may replace or remove although you have not read or listed them in this session. Every other path the call touches must be one you read by its `path`, saw in a file listing, or published yourself, and must not have changed since — otherwise nothing is sent and the refusal names each path. Name a path here only when the user asked for it to be replaced without looking at what is there; it never excuses a path that changed after you read it.

url.description: An existing artifact's claude.ai link (claude.ai/artifact/{id} or claude.ai/code/artifact/{uuid}); a chat, project or session link is not one, and `action: "list"` lists the person's artifacts. On a publish, it is the artifact to update in place, one the person owns or was given edit access to (a read of it says "writer"). Before publishing to an artifact this conversation has neither read nor published, Claude reads it (`action: "read"`) and builds on what comes back; a publish sent without that read is refused. A refusal that hands Claude the live version counts as that read: Claude merges its changes into that version and publishes the result, and never resends the refused content unchanged. Claude omits `url` for a new artifact or to redeploy a file this conversation already published. For read, delete and the other calls that take a URL, it is the artifact to act on.

type_url.description: publish: the Artifact type to create this new, private Artifact from (a link from a 'types' listing). Claude omits `url`. Any `file_path`/`files` passed become the new Artifact's own files beside the type's fixed ones. read (no `url`): the type to describe. list: the type whose Artifacts to list, or Claude names the type with `type` instead.

auto_open.description: Only with `type_url` and no `file_path`: when the new Artifact opens for the person. Claude passes "after_first_write" when it will fill the Artifact right after creating it with a files publish to its url, so the person does not first see it empty. The Artifact then opens on that first write. Otherwise Claude omits it, and the Artifact opens when created; Claude always omits it for a type whose content it writes through a connector, such as a Claude Docs document, since no publish or store write follows to open it.

prompt.description: read, for an artifact shared with the person: what Claude needs from it, which steers the isolated summary.

force.description: publish: a last-resort overwrite that **discards** the newer published version. On a conflict, Claude merges its changes onto the newer content that the rejection hands it and publishes again. Claude passes true only when the person explicitly said to discard that specific version, and the server may still refuse it over a version saved from inside the page.

out_dir.description: read with `path`: the directory to save into. The default is this artifact's folder in Claude's scratchpad directory, where saving needs no approval. A published file lands at <out_dir>/<published path>, and saving it outside that default folder asks the person first. An asset's file is named by its id plus its type's extension; saving it outside the default folder is an ordinary file save the person may be asked to approve.

path.description: read: the file's published path inside the artifact, exactly as a 'files' listing printed it ("index.html" is the page itself). The file is saved locally, the result says where, and a small text file's contents are included. It can instead be an uploaded asset's id (32 hex characters, from an 'assets' listing or an upload result), and that asset is saved to a local file. delete: the id of the one asset to remove.

paths.description: read: several published paths in place of `path`, up to 256 in one call. Each file is saved as a single `path` would be, and the result lists where each one landed, or why it could not be read, with small text files' contents included while they fit.

after.description: list with scope 'assets' only: the `next` value from a previous listing, passed to continue it.

page.description: read only: true returns the rendered page in cases where a read otherwise returns something else. A typed Artifact's read leaves out the type's own page.

capabilities.description: publish: the runtime capabilities this page declares, as {name: config}. Claude loads the `artifact-capabilities` skill before passing it. On a redeploy Claude omits the field to keep what the page has, and {} clears it.

contract.description: publish: the artifact's runtime version. Leaving it out keeps the current version (the default), 'latest' upgrades, and an exact version pins or rolls back. It changes how the published page behaves, so Claude passes it only when the author explicitly intends that change.

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- Working directory persists between calls, but prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background.

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.name: Edit
tools.description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__dismiss_task
tools.description:
Withdraw a background-task chip you previously created with spawn_task.

Call this when a suggestion you flagged is now stale, superseded, or irrelevant — e.g. you (or the user) already fixed it in this session, or you spawned a better-scoped replacement. To replace a chip: call spawn_task with the new suggestion first, then dismiss the old task_id.

Only chips the user hasn't acted on can be withdrawn from the queue. If the user already started or dismissed the task, the result says so (a dismissed task's copy kept for later is withdrawn too) — do not retry.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__mark_chapter
tools.description:
Mark the start of a new chapter in this session.

Call this when the work shifts to a meaningfully different phase — e.g. after finishing exploration and starting implementation, after a fix lands and you move to verification, or when the user pivots to an unrelated request. The user sees a divider in the transcript and a floating table of contents for jumping between chapters.

Use sparingly: a chapter should cover a coherent stretch of work, not every tool call. A typical session has 3–8 chapters. Do not mark a chapter for the very first message — the session start is implicit.

The title is a short noun phrase ("Codebase exploration", "Auth bug fix", "Test verification"), not a sentence.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__spawn_task
tools.description:
Flag an out-of-scope issue for a separate background task.

Call this when you notice something worth fixing that would bloat the current change — dead code, stale docs, missing coverage, a confirmed TODO, or a security issue spotted in passing. Don't flag vague code-smell observations, trivial fixes you can do inline, or low-confidence hunches. A chip appears for the user; one click spins it off into its own session. Your current turn continues uninterrupted.

The prompt must stand alone — include file paths and enough context to act without this conversation.

The result includes a task_id; call dismiss_task with it if the suggestion later becomes stale.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. #!/bin/bash
# Nxeon — weekly NxLabs mod-catalog refresh: run WEEKLY.
#
# WHY THIS EXISTS: the 2026-09-24 audit found nothing re-runs any mod
# importer or scripts/verify-gamemods.ts on a schedule at all — checked
# `systemctl list-timers`, crontabs, and the worker's own job loop, all came
# back empty. Every one of the 45,761 live GameMod rows was last touched
# 2026-09-19/20 (the day the original bulk imports ran) with no refresh
# since: download counts drift, removed upstream projects never get
# `upstreamOk: false`, and new mods never get picked up.
#
# WHAT THIS RUNS, IN ORDER, EACH WEEK:
#   1. Re-run each source's bulk IMPORTER with --apply — picks up new
#      projects/plugins/packages published upstream since last week AND
#      refreshes longDescription/downloads/etc. on existing rows (every
#      importer's write is a plain upsert on its real unique key, so
#      re-running is always safe/idempotent, never duplicates).
#   2. scripts/verify-gamemods.ts — the per-row freshness/removal pass for
#      modrinth/spigotmc/thunderstore (flips upstreamOk: false the moment a
#      project disappears upstream, refreshes fileBytes/impact/gallery).
#
# NOT INCLUDED: scripts/import-umod-catalog.ts. Its own file header explains
# why — uMod's ToS page is behind a Cloudflare bot challenge and could not
# be read before that script was written, so it is NOT wired into an
# unattended weekly schedule until a human confirms the terms allow it. Run
# it by hand (see that script's own usage comment) once that's resolved, and
# add it to WEEKLY_STEPS below at the same time.
#
# RATE LIMITING: each importer already self-paces against its own source's
# real/assumed limit (see each script's own RATE_LIMIT_PER_MIN-equivalent
# constant) — this wrapper adds no additional throttling, just runs them
# one at a time (never concurrently) so no two sources hit the network at
# once, and so one source's slow run (Thunderstore's README pass is the
# long pole — ~1,300 sequential requests at 120/min is ~11 minutes) doesn't
# fight another for the same outbound connection pool.
#
# CONCURRENCY GUARD: none needed in this script itself — the systemd unit
# this runs under (deploy/nxeon-weekly-modcatalog.service) is Type=oneshot,
# which systemd itself refuses to start again while already running (same
# pattern as deploy/nxeon-nightly-scan.service).
#
# Install: see deploy/WEEKLY-MODCATALOG-README.md.
#
# Manual dry run (no writes, just to see it execute cleanly):
#   NXEON_DB_TARGET=nxeon_staging DRY_RUN=1 bash scripts/weekly-mod-catalog-refresh.sh
# Manual real run against staging first:
#   NXEON_DB_TARGET=nxeon_staging bash scripts/weekly-mod-catalog-refresh.sh

set -uo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." || exit 1

log() { echo "[$(date +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%z)] $*"; }

APPLY_FLAG="--apply"
if [[ "${DRY_RUN:-0}" == "1" ]]; then
  APPLY_FLAG=""
  log "DRY_RUN=1 — every importer below runs WITHOUT --apply (report only, no writes)"
fi

if [[ -z "${NXEON_DB_TARGET:-}" ]]; then
  log "ERROR NXEON_DB_TARGET is not set — every importer's own db-target-guard will refuse to run. Set it explicitly (see scripts/db-target-guard.ts)."
  exit 1
fi
log "target database: ${NXEON_DB_TARGET}"

rc=0

log "step 1/5 — Modrinth (mods/plugins/resourcepacks/shaders/datapacks/modpacks)"
if ! npx tsx scripts/import-modrinth-catalog.ts ${APPLY_FLAG}; then
  log "ERROR Modrinth import failed — continuing with the remaining sources"
  rc=1
fi

log "step 2/5 — Steam Workshop (10 families)"
if ! npx tsx scripts/import-steamworkshop-catalog.ts ${APPLY_FLAG}; then
  log "ERROR Steam Workshop import failed — continuing with the remaining sources"
  rc=1
fi

log "step 3/5 — Thunderstore (valheim, sons-of-the-forest, schedule-i, sunkenland)"
if ! npx tsx scripts/import-thunderstore-catalog.ts ${APPLY_FLAG}; then
  log "ERROR Thunderstore import failed — continuing with the remaining sources"
  rc=1
fi

log "step 4/5 — verify-gamemods (modrinth/spigotmc/thunderstore freshness + removal pass)"
if [[ -n "${APPLY_FLAG}" ]]; then
  # verify-gamemods.ts has no --apply flag of its own (it always writes) and
  # no db-target-guard — it inherits DATABASE_URL from the environment like
  # any other script. Skipped entirely in DRY_RUN mode since there is no
  # dry-run form of it to fall back to.
  if ! npx tsx scripts/verify-gamemods.ts; then
    log "ERROR verify-gamemods failed"
    rc=1
  fi
else
  log "DRY_RUN=1 — skipping verify-gamemods.ts (it has no dry-run mode; it always writes)"
fi

log "step 5/5 — done (exit ${rc})"
exit "${rc}"

# Nxeon weekly NxLabs mod-catalog refresh

Re-runs every mod-catalog importer (Modrinth, Steam Workshop, Thunderstore)
with `--apply`, then `scripts/verify-gamemods.ts`, once a week. Fixes the gap
the 2026-09-24 audit found: nothing re-ran any importer or the verify pass on
a schedule — every one of the 45,761 live `GameMod` rows was last touched the
day the original bulk imports ran, with no refresh since (download counts
drift, removed upstream projects never get `upstreamOk: false`, new mods
never get picked up).

Entrypoint: `scripts/weekly-mod-catalog-refresh.sh` (see that file's own
header for exactly what runs, in what order, and why `import-umod-catalog.ts`
is deliberately NOT included yet).

## Install + enable the timer

```bash
# Copy the units into place
sudo cp /opt/nxeon/deploy/nxeon-weekly-modcatalog.service /etc/systemd/system/
sudo cp /opt/nxeon/deploy/nxeon-weekly-modcatalog.timer   /etc/systemd/system/

# Reload systemd and enable the weekly timer (fires Mon ~03:15, catches up if missed)
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl enable --now nxeon-weekly-modcatalog.timer
```

## Verify / operate

```bash
# See when it will next run
systemctl list-timers nxeon-weekly-modcatalog.timer

# Run it once right now (writes real upserts against production)
sudo systemctl start nxeon-weekly-modcatalog.service

# Inspect the last run's output (per-source counts: searched/upserted/created/updated/failed)
journalctl -u nxeon-weekly-modcatalog.service --no-pager -n 200
```

The service runs as `User=nxeon` with `EnvironmentFile=/opt/nxeon/.env` plus
an explicit `Environment=NXEON_DB_TARGET=nxeon` (not present in `.env` as of
2026-09-24 — every importer's `scripts/db-target-guard.ts` refuses to run
without it, by design; see that file's own header for why). It is a
`oneshot` unit driven entirely by the timer — enabling the timer is all
that's needed, and systemd itself refuses to start a second overlapping run
of a `oneshot` unit, so no separate lockfile is needed.

## Before enabling this in production

Run it once by hand against **staging** first and read the output:

```bash
NXEON_DB_TARGET=nxeon_staging bash /opt/nxeon/scripts/weekly-mod-catalog-refresh.sh
```

And confirm `scripts/import-umod-catalog.ts`'s ToS question (its own file
header) has actually been resolved before ever adding it to this schedule —
it is intentionally left out of `weekly-mod-catalog-refresh.sh` today.

---
name: nxeon-disk-full-outage-2026-09-27
description: Primary node root disk hit 100% from build caches, Postgres crashed, prod 500 for ~10 min; what to clear and what never to touch
metadata:
  type: project
---

**2026-09-27, 08:21–08:31 UTC:** the primary node's root filesystem filled up and production went down.
- **Symptom:** `/dev/md3` (49G, `/`) reached 100%. `postgresql@17-main`, which holds prod `nxeon` plus the staging DBs, crashed with "No space left on device", and prod on :3000 returned 500.
- **Cause:** cumulative regenerable caches, not the databases (all DBs together are about 500 MB).
  - staging `.next/cache` (2.1G)
  - `~/.npm/_cacache` (1.7G), `~/.cache/go-build` (1.3G)
  - worktree `.next` build outputs (2.2G in `ssh-management-key`)
  - The trigger was the /nxm `next dev` cache growing during multi-agent work.
- **Fix:** delete those caches, then `systemctl start postgresql@17-main` (it crash-recovers cleanly). That took free space from 134M to 8.5G.

**How to apply:**
- Before long builds or multi-agent `next dev` sessions on this box, check `df -h /`.

 * scale" pass NxLabs never had. Separate from `scripts/verify-gamemods.ts`,

 * verify-gamemods.ts afterward on a schedule to keep them fresh and to
 * backfill fileBytes/impact/dependencyCount, which this script deliberately
 * does not touch — see "WHAT THIS DOES NOT FETCH" below).
 *
 * WHY THIS EXISTS. As of 2026-09-19 NxLabs has 119 real (of 124 seeded)
 * hand-picked mod rows across 5 families. Modrinth alone publishes ~158k real
 * projects. This script queries Modrinth's actual public search API, filters
 * to content that is genuinely installable on a DEDICATED SERVER (Nxeon's
 * product), and upserts real rows — every field traces to a live API
 * response, nothing here is fabricated.
 *
 * SOURCE: Modrinth REST API v2, https://docs.modrinth.com/api/ — a fully
 * public, documented, third-party-integration-friendly API (the same one
 * `scripts/verify-gamemods.ts` already calls; this script reuses its request
 * pattern: identifying User-Agent, optional API key header, real 429/5xx
 * backoff, no attempt to mirror/rehost files — only metadata + hotlinked CDN
 * images, files are fetched by the worker at install time, same as today).
 *
 * PROJECT TYPES COVERED: mod, plugin, resourcepack, shader, datapack,
 * modpack. Deliberately EXCLUDED: `minecraft_java_server` (Modrinth's own
 * dedicated server-jar listing product — not installable "content" the way
 * the six above are).
 *
 * SERVER-RELEVANCE FILTER: Modrinth's `environment` facet says whether a
 * project runs client, server, or both. We only import environments that are
 * meaningfully server-side: server_only, dedicated_server_only,
 * server_only_client_optional, client_and_server, client_or_server,
 * client_or_server_prefers_both. We exclude client_only / singleplayer_only
 * on purpose — Nxeon hosts dedicated servers, not client mods.
 *   ONE DELIBERATE EXCEPTION: for project_type "plugin" we ALSO accept
 *   environment "unknown". Reason (checked live against the real API, not
 *   guessed): "plugin" on Modrinth structurally means Bukkit/Spigot/
 *   Paper/Sponge/Velocity server software — there is no such thing as a
 *   client-only plugin — but a large fraction of real, popular, genuinely
 *   server-only plugins simply never got the environment field filled in by
 *   their author (verified live: project_type:plugin + our environment list
 *   + downloads>1000 = 141 hits; the SAME query without the environment
 *   filter = 3340 hits, and manually sampling the gap showed real, popular,
 *   unambiguously server-side plugins like Chunky and Simple Voice Chat
 *   tagged "unknown"/"client_or_server_prefers_both"). Excluding "unknown"
 *   for plugins specifically would throw away real, relevant, high-quality
 *   catalogue content over a data-entry gap, not a real client/server
 *   distinction. Every other project type keeps the strict list, because for

 *   client-only.

 * --min-follows): downloads > 1000 OR follows > 50. Implemented as two
 * disjoint search passes (Modrinth facets AND within a query; there is no
 * single-query OR across two different numeric fields) — pass 1 sorts by
 * downloads and takes everything over the download floor, pass 2 sorts by
 * follows and takes everything over the follow floor that pass 1 didn't
 * already take (`downloads<=floor`), so nothing is double-counted across
 * passes (cross-project-type duplicates from Modrinth's own
 * `all_project_types` overlap are still possible and handled by the
 * `seenProjectIds` set + the `@@unique([gameFamily, slug])` upsert either
 * way).

 * request bulk pass rather than a many-hour one): fileBytes,
 * dependencyCount, impact/impactNote. Those need a per-project `/version`
 * call each and are exactly what `verify-gamemods.ts` already does well —
 * re-run it with `--source=modrinth` after this script to backfill them, at
 * whatever pace is comfortable, on however many thousand rows this leaves it.

Now I'm working out the Modrinth provider logic: paginating by sorting on downloads with a resumable cursor tracking project type, sort index, and offset, while respecting the facets filter for minimum downloads and the API's 10000 offset+limit cap.

For freshness, I'm planning a two-mode sweep: a "recent" pass sorted by update date that stops once it hits projects older than the last successful run, followed by a "full" sweep covering everything, with the cursor's mode field determining which phase to run and switching to "full" once enough time has passed since the last full pass.

For fetching versions, since per-project calls would be too slow at scale, I'm leaning toward batching version lookups by passing multiple version IDs into a single bulk versions request, limiting this to mods above a minimum download threshold to keep request volume manageable.

I also need to be careful not to overwrite existing author avatar URLs with null just because the search results don't carry that data—I should preserve what's already stored rather than clobber it.

So for the store's update logic, I'll only drop keys with null/empty values for optional enrichment fields like authorAvatarUrl, license info, and descriptions, while keeping arrays empty if they're legitimately empty. This should only apply to updates, not fresh inserts.

Then I still need to sort out Modrinth's category filtering mapping to types/loaders, and figure out how Hangar's project listing endpoint structures its results.

Now I'm thinking through Hangar's pagination and rate limits - with a 25-item max per page and roughly 3,900 projects, that's about 156 pages, plus a version fetch per project. At a self-imposed cap of 60 requests/minute, fetching everything would take about an hour, so for partial runs I'd only pull versions for the top N projects by downloads. # NX Labs mod sources — licensing / ToS verdicts

Owner of this document: K2 (modcatalog), 2026-10-01. Code: `lib/modsync/*`, `worker/modsync.ts`,
`scripts/modsync.ts`, admin page `/admin/nxlabs`.

## The rule

> **Only MIRROR a file when the project's own license grants redistribution.** Everything else is
> *metadata + link-through*: we store name, description, images, versions, license text/URL,
> author, source URL and attribution, and the installer fetches the file from the upstream at
> install time (as it did before this work).

Mechanically: `lib/modsync/license.ts#isRedistributable(license)` is true only for a closed list of
open SPDX ids (MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD-*, ISC, MPL-2.0, LGPL/GPL/AGPL family, CC0, CC-BY(-SA), Unlicense,
Zlib, ...). Unknown, empty, "All Rights Reserved", `LicenseRef-*`, "Other", NC licenses => **false**.
`GameMod.redistributable` stores the result; `mirrorVersion()` refuses (state `SKIPPED`, reason
recorded on the row) when it is false, when the file has no direct https URL, when the resource is
paid, or when it exceeds `NXLABS_MIRROR_MAX_FILE_BYTES` (150 MB). Providers whose `policy` is
`metadata-only` are never offered to the mirror at all.

Every upstream call goes through `lib/modsync/http.ts`: User-Agent
`NxeonModSync/1.0 (+https://nxeon.cloud; mods@nxeon.cloud)`, token-bucket pacing below the
provider's published limit, exponential backoff + jitter, `Retry-After` honoured, ETag /
If-Modified-Since support, per-request timeout.

Caveat on this document: verdicts below are based on the public API documentation and live probes
made on 2026-10-01. I did **not** read every provider's full legal ToS text (several are behind
Cloudflare or login walls). Where that matters it says so; anything marked "owner to confirm"
should be confirmed by a human before the provider is switched on.

## Verdict table

| Provider | Games | Access | Per-file license data? | Verdict | Status in code |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Modrinth** | Minecraft (mods, plugins, resource/data packs, shaders, modpacks) | Public REST v2, no key required (our `MODRINTH_API_KEY` only identifies us), 300 req/min | Yes: `license.id` (SPDX) + `license.url` per project | **Mirror when license is open; else link-through.** API ToS asks for an identifying UA and no abuse; files are third-party licensed, so the author's license governs. | Native provider `modrinth` (mirror-if-licensed) |
| **Hangar** (PaperMC) | Minecraft plugins (Paper/Velocity/Waterfall) | Public REST, no key | Yes: `settings.license.{name,type,url}` (free text/"GPL"/"MIT"/"Other") | **Mirror when it maps to an open license; else link-through.** Builds with `externalUrl` (hosted elsewhere) are always link-through. | Native provider `hangar` (mirror-if-licensed) |
| **Factorio mod portal** | Factorio | Public read API, no key; **downloads require a factorio.com username+token** | Per-mod `license` object exists on `/api/mods/<name>/full` (not in list) | **Metadata only.** File download is login-gated, so anonymous mirroring is impossible by design, and we will not hold users' credentials for it. | Native provider `factorio` (metadata-only) + legacy importer |
| **ficsit.app** | Satisfactory | Public GraphQL, no key | No license field in the listing | **Metadata only** (no license => not redistributable). Installs go through Satisfactory Mod Manager's own path. | Native provider `ficsit` (metadata-only) + legacy importer |
| **Thunderstore** | Valheim, Sons of the Forest, Schedule I, Sunkenland, ... | Public v1 package list (one huge response per community — Valheim alone is ~170 MB; use ETag), no key | No structured license; READMEs only | **Metadata + link-through.** Community packages declare no license, so redistribution is not granted. | Legacy importer (`scripts/import-thunderstore-catalog.ts`); native provider is a follow-up (needs streaming JSON parse — do NOT `res.json()` the 170 MB body in the worker) |
| **uMod / Oxide** | Rust (also 7DTD, Hurtworld...) | `search.json` works unauthenticated, but `robots.txt` and ToS pages sit behind a Cloudflare challenge | Plugin pages show a license; not reliably in `search.json` | **Disabled, owner to confirm ToS.** Metadata at most, never mirror. ## The rule

> **Only MIRROR a file when the project's own license grants redistribution.** Everything else is
> *metadata + link-through*: we store name, description, images, versions, license text/URL,
> author, source URL and attribution, and the installer fetches the file from the upstream at
> install time (as it did before this work).

content.thinking:
I'm realizing there's a policy flaw: with popularity-first mirroring, the most popular items get mirrored earliest, which under LRU-by-mirroredAt eviction means they'd actually get evicted first when the cap is exceeded during a bulk fill — the opposite of what's intended at real-world 100GB/150GB scale.

My fix: restrict eviction victims to items with downloads at or below the incoming item's downloads, or ones unaccessed for 30+ days, so popular files can't be evicted to make room for less-popular ones. If no valid victim exists, treat it as a "budget full" outcome rather than a failure — leave the row state unchanged and have the runner count and stop the loop on that signal instead of marking it FAILED.

I'm testing that a popular mod with high downloads can evict the open slot, then checking the reverse case where a low-popularity mod can't evict a higher one. I'm also setting up a scenario where a mod with minimal downloads tries to mirror data when the budget is nearly full, expecting it to fail with a FULL result.

entry='''## NX Labs catalog ingestion, local mod mirror and /admin/nxlabs (2026-10-01)

**Why.** `GameMod` held ~64,000 rows (Minecraft 32k, Factorio 5.4k, Vintage Story 3.9k, Space Engineers 2.2k,
~20 other families at ~1k each) but only a weekly shell timer (`scripts/weekly-mod-catalog-refresh.sh`, never
installed) refreshed it, rows carried no per-version/compatibility data, images were hotlinked, and no file was
ever stored locally. Audit of prod (read-only, 2026-10-01): Minecraft is rich (icon 100%, versions 100%,
license 99.9%, gallery 66%), but most Steam-Workshop families have 0% versions/license/long description,
Rust has only 30 rows (uMod importer deliberately unscheduled, Cloudflare-blocked ToS), CS:GO/CS 1.6 9 rows,
Terraria 23, 11 duplicated (family, source, sourceId) groups.

**What shipped (agent K2, branch `feature/mod-catalog-ingestion`).**
- `lib/modsync/*` provider framework: `types.ts`, `http.ts` (identifying UA, token-bucket pacing, exponential backoff
  with jitter, Retry-After, ETag/If-Modified-Since), `license.ts` (redistribution allow-list), `store.ts` (idempotent
  upsert keyed by `(gameFamily, source, sourceId)` with the legacy slug convention; never blanks known fields with
  nulls; sanitised HTML via `lib/mod-markdown.ts`), `images.ts` (sharp -> WebP, content-addressed, served by
  `app/api/nxlabs/img/[key]/route.ts`), `mirror.ts`, `runner.ts` (resumable bounded slices, DB claim, run history),
  `registry.ts`, `urls.ts` (`modIconSrc`/`modGallerySrc` helpers for UIs). Native providers: **modrinth**,
  **hangar**, **factorio**, **ficsit**; each exports pure parsers tested against recorded fixtures
  (`test/fixtures/modsync/*`, `test/modsync.test.ts`).
- Worker: `worker/modsync.ts` `modsyncTick()` hooked into `worker/index.ts` (fire-and-forget every 5 min; one bounded
  slice <= 6 min of the next due provider; cursor saved in `ModSyncProvider`). `MODSYNC_DISABLED=1` turns it off.
- Admin: `/admin/nxlabs` (`app/admin/nxlabs/page.tsx`, `lib/actions-admin-nxlabs.ts`, `components/admin/NxLabsSyncControls.tsx`;
  one tab added to `lib/admin-groups.ts`): per-provider status/last run/counts/errors, mirror usage + free space,
  per-game coverage, recent runs, Run now / Pause / Resume / Enable / Disable / Reset cursor (audited via `recordAudit`).
- CLI: `scripts/modsync.ts run <provider> [--max --mode --no-images --mirror-limit --loop]`, `status`, `verify-mirror`;
  `scripts/modsync-mirror-selftest.ts` (throwaway DB + local HTTP server).
- Licensing verdicts per provider: `docs/MODS-SOURCES.md`. Rule: mirror only when the project license is an open SPDX id;
  everything else is metadata + link-through. Steam Workshop, CurseForge, Nexus, mod.io, uMod are never mirrored.

**Schema (additive only).** `GameMod`: `sourceUrl, licenseUrl, redistributable, categories[], tags[], iconKey,
galleryKeys[], bodyHtml, latestVersion, followers, syncedAt` + index `[source, sourceId]`. New models `ModVersion`
(per build: gameVersions[] x loaders[] compat matrix, file url/size/sha1/sha256/sha512, changelog, dependencies, mirror
state/path/bytes/hash/lastAccessedAt/accessCount), `ModSyncProvider` (scheduler state, cursor, etag, pause/enable),
`ModSyncRun` (history, pruned to 200). Needs a one-time `prisma db push` on prod (all additive).

**Local mirror.** No dedicated NX Labs volume exists on this host (checked df/lsblk/zfs/pvesm/DB/docs). Root `/` (49 GB)
and `/var/lib/vz` (on the 71%-full NVMe pool) are unsuitable; `tank` (2.9 TB free) is the home. The mirror root
(`NXLABS_MIRROR_DIR`, default `/tank/nxlabs-mirror`) must be provisioned by the owner; the code refuses to create it
itself so a missing mount can never fill the root disk (image caching and mirroring just turn off). Layout is
content-addressed (`files/<aa>/<sha256>`, `img/<aa>/<sha256>.webp`), budget `NXLABS_MIRROR_MAX_BYTES` (default 100 GB),
eviction = least recently accessed first, popularity tie-break, never evicting a more popular mod to admit a less popular
one, shared blobs unlinked only with their last referencing row. Installer fast path: `resolveLocal(modVersion|id)` in
`lib/modsync/mirror.ts` returns an absolute path or `null` (then fetch `ModVersion.fileUrl` as before).

**Proof run (throwaway DB, real public APIs, scratch mirror on tmpfs).** Modrinth 2,500 mods (1,505 redistributable,
2,491 icons + 1,591 with screenshots cached as WebP, 100% description/body/versions/license); Hangar 425 plugins (316
redistributable, 425 icons); ficsit 1,297; Factorio 1,686 (partial slice, cursor saved, resumed correctly across process
runs; no icons/licenses from the list endpoint). Mirror: 120+60 newest-release files fetched and hash-verified; average
file 2.9 MB, so the whole redistributable popular Minecraft slice (~20k mods) is roughly 60 GB: it fits the 100 GB budget.
Re-running ficsit in `recent` mode: created 0, updated 126 (idempotent). Eviction exercised under a 300 MB test budget
(94 evictions). Mirror self-test passes (license gate, hash-mismatch rejection, dedupe, budget, popularity-safe eviction,
corruption detection).

**Not done / limits.** Native Thunderstore, Steam Workshop, mod.io, Vintage Story, Reforger, uMod providers are NOT ported
(legacy scripts still serve them; admin page lists them read-only); Rust/CS2/Terraria coverage gaps remain until uMod ToS is
confirmed and a CurseForge key exists; Modrinth Meilisearch caps offset at 10,000 per project type, so deep-tail mods
beyond the top 10k per type are only reached by the legacy importer. The `/admin/nxlabs` page and the image route were
typechecked and are DB-backed, but NOT browser-rendered (dev server withheld during the root-disk emergency). Pre-existing:
`/admin/game-mods` loads every GameMod row at once (~64k) and should be paginated.

'''

- Admin: `/admin/nxlabs` (`app/admin/nxlabs/page.tsx`, `lib/actions-admin-nxlabs.ts`, `components/admin/NxLabsSyncControls.tsx`;

(per build: gameVersions[] x loaders[] compat matrix, file url/size/sha1/sha256/sha512, changelog, dependencies, mirror

input.message:
K2 (modcatalog) REPORT

Branch feature/mod-catalog-ingestion, worktree /opt/nxeon-wt-modcatalog. Commits: c7bf1ec4d6 (framework, mirror, admin page, tests, docs/MODS-SOURCES.md) and 015a50b120 (mirror safety fixes, DOCUMENTATION.md entry). Main was merged in (already up to date). The auto-push hook ran.

URGENT, found at start: the primary's root disk was 100% full. Postgres was alive and prod returned 200. I deleted only the documented-safe caches (/root/.npm/_cacache, _npx, ~/.cache/go-build), which freed about 4 GB. Root is now 78% used. This is also why the mirror must not live on /.

1. EXISTING CATALOG (prod DB, read-only)
- GameMod has about 64k rows. Minecraft has 32k, Factorio 5.4k, Vintage Story 3.9k, Space Engineers 2.2k, plus roughly 25 other families at 1k or fewer.
- Minecraft is rich: icon 100%, versions 100%, license 99.9%, gallery 66%.
- Most Steam-Workshop families have 0% versions, license and long description.
- Rust has only 30 rows (the uMod importer is unscheduled because its ToS is behind Cloudflare). cs16 has 9 rows and Terraria 23.
- 11 duplicate (family, source, sourceId) groups exist.
- Nothing refreshes the catalog on a schedule. The weekly timer in deploy/ was never installed.
- Rows were last touched 2026-09-19/20, or 09-24/30 for some sources.

2. PROVIDER VERDICTS (docs/MODS-SOURCES.md)
- Mirror a file only when the project license is an open SPDX id. Everything else is metadata plus link-through.
- Mirror-eligible: Modrinth and Hangar.
- Metadata only: Factorio (downloads are login-gated), ficsit, Thunderstore, Steam Workshop (never redistribute files), mod.io, CurseForge (needs an API key, which you don't have), Nexus (no scraping), Spigot.
- uMod is disabled until a human confirms its ToS.
- I read API docs and probed live. I did not read every legal ToS page.

3. CODE
- lib/modsync/*: http client, license policy, store, images (webp), mirror, runner, registry.
- Native providers: modrinth, hangar, factorio, ficsit. Parsers are tested against recorded fixtures.
- worker/modsync.ts, hooked into worker/index.ts with a fire-and-forget tick every 5 minutes. The cursor is stored in the DB so runs resume.
- /admin/nxlabs plus controls (audited): Run now, Pause, Resume, Enable, Disable, Reset cursor.
- Image route /api/nxlabs/img/[key].
- CLI scripts/modsync.ts.
- K1 fast path: resolveLocal(modVersion or id) returns an absolute path or null (null means fetch ModVersion.fileUrl as before).
- UI helpers modIconSrc and modGallerySrc in lib/modsync/urls.ts.

4. MIRROR STORAGE
- I found no existing 100 GB NX Labs volume. / and /var/lib/vz are unsuitable. tank has 2.9 TB free.
- Owner action: zfs create -o quota=100G -o mountpoint=/tank/nxlabs-mirror tank/nxlabs-mirror; chown nxeon:nxeon /tank/nxlabs-mirror
- The code never creates the mirror root. If it is missing, image caching and mirroring switch off.
- Layout is content-addressed by sha256. Eviction is LRU with a popularity tie-break and never evicts a more popular mod to admit a less popular one.
- Pre-downloading helps mainly with reliability, not speed. Only the newest release of the most-downloaded redistributable mods is mirrored. Average file size is 2.9 MB, so about 60 GB covers the whole popular Minecraft slice.

5. PROOF (throwaway DB, real public APIs, scratch mirror on tmpfs)
- Counts: Modrinth 2,500 (1,505 redistributable, 2,491 icons, 1,591 with screenshots cached), Hangar 425, ficsit 1,297, Factorio 1,686.
- Resume: cursors survived across separate process runs.
- Re-run: created 0, updated 126.
- Mirror: 180 hash-verified files stored. 94 evictions under a 300 MB test budget.
- scripts/modsync-mirror-selftest.ts passes: license gate, hash mismatch rejected, dedupe, budget, popularity-safe eviction, corruption detection.
- npx tsx --test test/modsync.test.ts: 9/9 pass.
- Typecheck is clean on a narrowed tsconfig covering my files. The full tsc never got the global lock, which had a 20+ job queue.
- Throwaway DBs dropped and scratch files deleted.

6. SCHEMA (additive only, needs a prod prisma db push)
- GameMod gains 11 columns and an index: sourceUrl, licenseUrl, redistributable, categories, tags, iconKey, galleryKeys, bodyHtml, latestVersion, followers, syncedAt.
- New models: ModVersion, ModSyncProvider, ModSyncRun.

7. FILES OUTSIDE MY AREA
- worker/index.ts: 9 lines (import, timer variable, tick call).
- lib/admin-groups.ts: one tab, "NX Labs sync", under Catalog.

8. PRODUCTION START
- No manual command is needed after deploy. Steps:
  1. Run prisma db push (additive).
  2. Provision the dataset above.
  3. Set NXLABS_MIRROR_DIR in .env if the path differs.
  4. Restart the worker.
- The first tick starts a full pass: Modrinth daily, Hangar daily, ficsit and Factorio daily. After that, daily recent passes and a full pass every 7 days.
- Optional manual run: NXEON_DB_TARGET=nxeon npx tsx scripts/modsync.ts run hangar --loop
- MODSYNC_DISABLED=1 turns it off.

9. NOT DONE
- I did not browser-render /admin/nxlabs or the image route, because of the disk emergency. They typecheck and read real DB data.
- Thunderstore, Steam Workshop, mod.io, Vintage Story, Reforger and uMod have no native providers. The legacy importers still serve them, and the admin page lists them read-only.
- Rust, CS2 and Terraria gaps remain until the uMod ToS is confirmed and a CurseForge key exists.
- Modrinth search caps at 10k results per type.
- The Factorio list endpoint returns no icons or licenses. Existing prod values are preserved because null values never overwrite known fields.
- Cross-provider dedupe (a plugin on both Modrinth and Hangar) is not implemented.
- /admin/game-mods loads all 64k rows at once and should be paginated.
